definition: Amicable means friendly and free of conflict, especially between parties who might have quarreled.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word amicable. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know amicable should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The two labs had raced each other for a decade, yet the merger talks stayed amicable from the first handshake to the last signature.
Civil stops short of amicable — civil rivals manage bare politeness at the door, while an amicable pair genuinely wishes each other well.
Harmonious goes further than amicable — amicable parties have settled their differences, while harmonious ones work so smoothly together that differences barely arise.

Peaceable describes a temperament — a person or nation disposed to avoid fighting in the first place. Amicable belongs to relations and agreements: it says the dealings between parties who might have quarreled stayed friendly. A peaceable neighbor avoids the dispute; an amicable settlement ends one on good terms.

Cooperative means willing to work together toward a shared task, and it can describe strangers with no history at all. Amicable implies more: goodwill between parties who could easily have fought — rivals, exes, opposing sides. A cooperative committee divides the work; an amicable split heals the expected conflict.
